en: They have an army and a Jang-Jung khan;
In swarming Kakan
There are creatures of many kinds.
If we follow the tradition,
If we ask those who know,
It has peoples of countless kinds;
Do not challenge them, my orphan,
For they have strength to engulf you.
My pale, soft young camel,
My goshawk, my morning star,
Saying, 'I shall campaign against Beijing,'
You have prepared for danger;
Saying, 'I shall campaign against Kakan,'
You have readied the rangy courser!"
Oh, my darling foal!
Beijing is no easy place,
Kakan-Chin is no easy people;
It has fortified passes,
It has the hero Kalcha,
And everyone who attacks it
It can cast into ruin.
Swarming like black beetles,
Kakan-Chin has its people,
And everyone who attacks it,
By custom, it drinks their blood.
Great Beijing, with its Kakan,
Whoever went there never returned.
To that great and imposing people,
No man ever made the journey;
Whoever attacked did not survive.
It has the people of forty tribes;
No one who faced them prevailed,
No one who advanced survived.
Beijing is no trifling place;
The seething unbelievers
Are no people a man can conquer.
It has a firmly fortified road,
And the mighty Kalcha hero,
Who never retreats once he advances.
The road to Beijing has five divisions;
If you seek it, its road is a great hell.
Oh, my beloved only son,
I have followed the tradition,
I have asked the learned men!
When the Flood surged and overflowed,
And all the world
It covered and overwhelmed,
Light poured upon Beijing,
And those people survived.
Beijing, untouched by a holy man,
Do not say, “I shall take it myself.”
Do not rave so!
In the Prophet's time,
Against Beijing and its Kakan
A holy war was waged there.
Men were gathered into an army,
And the whole force was made abundant.
They waged holy war against the Kakan,
But a saint saw then
How strongly Beijing was fortified.
If told, many sorrows emerge:
At that time, to Beijing
A multitude covering the earth went.
An army covering the world went,
No small host, but a great one.
From among those people there,
From Beijing, whose women were beautiful,
They took wives, and in Beijing
The Turks remained, it seems.
In the city of Chinmachin,
The Turks truly remained, it seems.
When we consider it, the grief is deep:
So many people remained in Beijing.
Descendants of the old Kyrgyz,
If you ask, you can find them;
Even to this day there remains
A people called the “Salaalyk.”
They made those who fought them fall,
Your strength is no match for Beijing;
Those who fought it did not return alive,
Your power is no match for Beijing.
Yesterday, my son, did the news reach you?
They took the road blessed by Khidr,
Your warrior father at their head,
An army of forty-two tumens went,
And in Beijing, untouched by Solomon,
When they were exacting judgment,
Your father Manas was a lion;
Among mortals, one like your father
The Creator who gives life
Will not soon grant again.
Your father Manas was a lionhearted hero;
In Beijing, untouched by a holy man,
There he inflicted suffering.
When it came time to load up, your lion father,
Your sharp-beaked one, could not understand;
Though I sat weeping and speaking,
He would not heed wretched me.
Gathering an army from among heroes,
Taking people and nation in abundance,
What I had said came to pass on that road:
They died in Kakan.
The great mullah who came from Mecca,
Many formidable khans died;
When they clashed in slaughter,
All the mighty ones died.
Your khan-father Manas, lionhearted hero,
Returned after fighting;
Which of them shall I name?
He lost the dear ones
Who had served as his support.
Your hero father, blessed by Khidr,
Entered without looking back and returned;
In the midst of the fierce battle,
He lost the warriors.
When your father began the war,
From the mountain side
Of high-cliffed Beijing they struck him;
The warriors suffered martyrdom,
And your dear father turned back.
Having become governor in Beijing,
He loaded and took much gold;
Then, without realizing it,
He lost the governors.
He grieved as he went on fighting;
Then your lion father
Lost his dear companions.
My lion son, hear this:
The Chinese tribes are a mighty people;
Many who marched to war
Met destruction there!
Imposing Beijing is the chief city;
Those who fought it saw true calamity.
When they went to the city of Chinmachin
To wage a true holy war,
There were formidable and able men,
Many mighty tigers among them.
In the midst of that war
There was old Bakai, blessed by Khidr;
As the slaughter raged,
There were many heroes in all.
Urging on his dun horse,
Your mighty father too was there.
Wise old Koshoy was there,
And all the heroes were there.
There were skillful spearmen,
And mighty wielders of battle-axes.
There were lions born exceptional,
Who did not shrink from death,
Who never turned back before dying;
There were heroes alongside your father,
There were peoples and their khans,
And there too was lion Alman,
Who knew every secret
Of Beijing and Kakan-Chin.
There was your precious khan-father,
In the midst of that war,
All forty companions were there.
From the dark and lowering Beijing,
When they went straight in and wrought slaughter,
They were steeped in the dust of chaos;
Without fleeing before the Kakan,
They fought unceasingly for six months.
When they went to that Beijing,
When they exacted judgment
From the Kakan whom none could touch,
As they withdrew from Beijing,
Your father had even Beijing,
Untouched by Chalyyar, struck down.
The reason he had it struck was this:
Muzburchak and Khan Kökchö died,
All who met the foe died.
The courageous gray-wolf giant died,
All who grappled with them died.
Only sons of their fathers died,
Many died with their hopes unfulfilled.
Precious lives beyond recovery died;
Before the seething unbelievers,
Before hero Khan Kongurbai,
All who fought died.
Those who met him did not return,
Those who encountered him did not escape alive.
When unbeliever and Muslim
Stood clashing together,
Such was the nature of that struggle.
Beijing is no easy place,
China is no easy people;
Your tiger father, the lion,
Entered Great Beijing and returned,
Having lost his tigers.
Your lion father exchanged fire,
Clashing with Beijing;
Your lion father grieved,
And while waging holy war against the Kakan,
He lost Khan Chubak,
Who had sat as his support.
Your father Manas, lionhearted hero,
Saw Akkula struck down by a bullet,
And Almambet suffer martyrdom;
He fought and returned,
And then your lion father
Lost those who had been his support.
Can Beijing be an easy place?
My heroic son, listen!
It has a desert forty days across,
And, as one ear has heard,
A people no man would wish to see.
Beijing is no easy place;
Your father Manas would not listen,
And led the armies of the world,
Leaving the village of sixty sons
And widowed women desolate!
Your wretched mother speaks—know this;
Oh, my only son, heed my words!
In teeming China,
There are the peoples of forty tribes;
Whoever attacks it, that Beijing
By custom drinks their blood.
Beijing is no easy place;
The Chinese are no people to toy with!
Mighty China is a powerful nation;
My dear son, know this:
When you see their multitude, they are black beetles!
If you wage holy war against the unbelievers,
My darling foal,
Hero Khan Kongurbai
Has a fortress beside the road;
The Kalcha whose road is barred
Has a lion who will answer you.
Do not dig my grave,
Forever refusing to listen;
Do not make my sorrows boil.
Forever refusing to heed
Your fathers and forefathers,
Do not show me such a spectacle!
My tiger son, hear my words!
Take able Bakai, who knows the road;
Take the stout-lunged, roaring,
The mighty who do not retreat from death,
Who spare themselves nothing.
Gather seven sacred banners,
Gather an army that makes the earth sag,
Then go to Beijing!
Take an army from the Muslims,
Take no small force, but many,
Then go to Beijing.
Fools merely say “Beijing”;
Those who know call it “Great Beijing”—
Beijing is no small place but vast.
On its front side is Bakburchun,
The mightiest of all is Kakan-Chin.
Most numerous is Shang-Kai, the great Manchu;
Consider how many cities there are.
If you ponder, that Beijing
Also has the aspect of a holy place.
